title: Ethiopian English Natural Stream Entrance 2017
description: Ethiopian English Natural Stream Entrance 2017 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText:
Section One: Reading Passage I

. Homeless people are everywhere on the street, in public buildings, on the evening news and in my morning dreams. The homeless are not just the dirty bums on the street. The homeless are not just constant symbols of our social failure. And above all, the homeless are not just bums.

2. What is the root of the homeless problem? Everyone seems to have a scapegoat. Advocates of the homeless blame the welfare system, politicians blame the system, the court, blame the bureaucratic infrastructure; the Democrats blame the Republicans and the Republicans blame the Democrats. The public blames three concepts: poverty, the \"poverty cycle,\" and the \"breakdown of society.\" With all this finger-pointing, the group that has become the most powerful has been overlooked by all of us: the bums. That group is the homeless themselves.

3. How can I say this? In the last two years I have worked with the homeless, volunteering at the Salvation Army and at a soup kitchen in Austin, Texas. I have led a seminar aimed at giving people good money management. Every time a morning cleared their struggles, I have seen their response to troubles, and though I would rather report successes, many of them seem to choose the life that requires the least. They are unwilling to do the things necessary to everyone their circumstances. They must bear the greatest part of the blame for their manifold troubles.

4. Let me qualify what I just said. Not everyone who finds himself out of a job and in the street is there because he has made a wrong choice. Among the more than three hundred many exhausted, sensible people during my time working with Austin's homeless: the father who is struggling to earn his bread and be a role model for his children; the woman who had a good job in another town, whose handsome husband drank up their savings and then had his world turned upside down by divorce and a layoff. These people deserve every effort to help them back on their feet.

5. But they are not the real problem. They are simply off the streets and resuming normal lives because union or welfare members even while others in need hide; they are responsible citizens, working in the shelters and applying for jobs. They are homeless, true but only temporarily because they are eager to recognize their lives.

6. For every person temporarily homeless, though there are many who are chronically so. Whether because of alcohol abuse, alcoholism, drug addiction, drug addiction or simply laziness, these homeless are content to remain as they are. In many cases they choose the street. They enjoy the freedom and camaraderie among themselves. And they bring the problems along: get a job for a day or two for food, cigarettes and alcohol. The problem, then, is not that we have failed to solve the poverty cycle, but to try and figure that a trip through the welfare line is less trouble than a steady job. In a society that has mastered a dodging responsibility, these homeless opt for a life of no responsibility at all.(Source: Critical Thinking, Thoughtful Writing: A Rhetoric with Readings by Chaffee, J. U.S.A (1999) (P.374-375).)

 Which one of the following statements is true according to paragraph 4?
options: Some homeless who are victims of circumstances deserve help to recognize their lives again.
None of those in the street deserve any effort to help them back on their feet.
woman fleeing an abusive husband is right away homeless.
Everyone who finds themselves out of a job is homeless.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 4 provides examples of people who are 'victims of circumstance' (like the father struggling to be a role model and the woman who lost everything due to divorce and layoff). 

It concludes by stating, 'These people deserve every effort to help them back on their feet.' Option A, 'Some homeless who are victims of circumstances deserve help to recognize their lives again,' is the closest paraphrase of this main idea in paragraph 4.

 Options B, C, and D are contradicted or not fully supported by the text in paragraph 4.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes this passage writer's tone?
questions.explanation:
The writer criticizes the government, the public, and even the homeless themselves (paragraphs 2, 3, 6).

 The tone is one of critical analysis and judgment of various parties' failures concerning the issue of homelessness.

questions.questionText: What does the expression 'I would rather report otherwise' indicate in the context it is used in paragraph 3?
options: The need to tell the public about the homeless
The fear to hide the true cause of homelessness
The need to explain the troubles facing the homeless
The fear to condemn the government for the problem
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 3, the writer discusses working with the homeless and notes, 'though I would rather report successes, many of them seem to choose the life that requires the least.'

 The phrase 'I would rather report otherwise' means the writer *wishes* they could report a different, more positive outcome (successes), but the reality they have to report is a negative one (the homeless choosing the path of least resistance). Therefore, the expression implies the author is compelled to tell the public an unpleasant truth they have observed.

questions.questionText: What purpose does the writer's reference to personal experience in paragraph 3 serve?
options: It served as evidence for political involvement.
It clarified the actual cause of homelessness.
It served as evidence of social disintegration.
It showed the ugly lifestyle of the homeless.
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 3, the writer describes personal experience working with the homeless, including volunteering and leading seminars.

 This is used to illustrate that, in many cases, the homeless themselves contribute to their circumstances by choosing the path of least resistance.

 The personal experience serves as concrete evidence to clarify that the causes of homelessness are not only external (society, economy) but also internal choices, helping the reader understand the actual dynamics behind homelessness.

questions.questionText: Which of the following words is closest in meaning to haggard as used in paragraph 1?
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 1, 'haggard' describes the appearance of homeless people on the streets.

 It conveys the sense of being worn out, tired, and destitute. 

Among the options, 'A person with no home' best captures the context-specific meaning of 'haggard' in this passage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following words can be synonymous with the word content as used in paragraph 6?
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 6, 'content' describes homeless people who choose to remain on the streets and are happy with their situation.

 Here, 'content' means 'satisfied' or 'pleased with their circumstances,' making 'satisfied' the correct synonym.

questions.questionText: What does the word there in paragraph 4, refer to?
questions.explanation: In paragraph 4, the author refers to people who find themselves 'out of a job and in the street.' The word 'there' in this context points to their location, which is 'in the street,' indicating homelessness or being without shelter.

questions.questionText: What does the word 'so' in paragraph 6, refer to?
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 6 begins: 'For every person temporarily homeless, though there are many who are chronically so.'

 The context is a discussion about people who are temporarily homeless versus those who are chronically homeless.

 Therefore, the word 'so' refers back to the state of being homeless.

questions.questionText: According to the passage, which of the following is to blame for the life of a homeless person?
questions.explanation:
The passage discusses multiple groups being blamed in paragraph 2 (politicians, bureaucracy, etc.), but the writer's own conclusion focuses on the homeless themselves.

 In paragraph 3, the writer states that many of them 'seem to choose the life that requires the least' and 'They must bear the greatest part of the blame for their manifold troubles.'

 The writer ultimately places the primary blame on The homeless themselves for choosing 'a life of no responsibility' (paragraph 6).

questions.questionText:
Section Two: Reading Passage II 
Environmental Protection

1. The preservation of forest areas, wildlife and soil should be of a vital concern to all Ethiopians. Failure to do so means a destruction of replaceable natural resources, a serious loss of revenue and then gradual desolation of the land until it becomes unfit for habitation. According to a UNEP survey in 1983, the consequences will be disastrous unless drastic measures are adopted. An example of this neglect is the present and past destruction of forests. In the good old days, the Ethiopian highlands were covered with virgin forests, which have since been largely used for construction and fuel. Along with the introduction of the eucalyptus, which covered the country with a misconception: a desert; however, the few remaining forest areas are not being preserved. The Ethiopian custom grants a man ownership of any land he clears of trees, and he is promised with forest lands as a reward for his service to the government. The next twenty or thirty years will see the last remnants of virgin forests destroyed unless strong measures are taken.

2. Soil degradation has been aggravated by poor agricultural practices. These include improper terracing, the cultivation of steep and easily eroded hillsides, failure to rotate crops (with the consequent loss of valuable nutrients), and the burning of manure instead of returning it to the soil as fertilizer. The destruction of trees and the lack of modern farming methods are not themselves as bad as the erosion of the soil which may follow them. Several generations may be able to live off the land, but gradually the soil is washed away to Egypt, making the land increasingly poor in quality and yielding less and less. Unfortunately, it is almost impossible to reclaim land that has deteriorated beyond a certain point. Trees cannot be planted to suck up water and hold the soil, because the earth is no longer deep enough to support long roots.(Source: College Writing Skills; A Reference and Practice Book, (2019), pp.61-63), 

 What does 'These' in paragraph 2 refer to?
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 states: 'Soil degradation has been aggravated by poor agricultural practices.

 These include improper terracing, the cultivation of steep and easily eroded hillsides...' The word 'These' is introducing the specific examples of the poor agricultural practices mentioned just before it.

 Therefore, 'These' refers to poor agricultural practices.

questions.questionText: What does the word desolation mean in paragraph 1?
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 1, 'desolation' describes the state of the homeless as isolated and abandoned.

 The closest meaning in this context is 'desertion,' which conveys being left alone or neglected.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best replaces the word 'aggravated' in paragraph 2?
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 states: 'Soil degradation has been aggravated by poor agricultural practices.'

 To aggravate means to make a problem, injury, or offense worse or more serious. Therefore, worsened is the best replacement.

questions.questionText: The prolonged erosion of the soil is followed by
options: enrichment of the soil by various nutrients.
questions.explanation: Prolonged soil erosion removes the top fertile layer of soil, making it difficult for plants to grow. Therefore, the immediate consequence is the total absence of plants rather than enrichment or animal reproduction.

questions.questionText: In highly eroded and desolated areas, trees fail to survive because
options: their roots are too short to suck up water from the ground.
the sun will be too scorching for them to survive.
they do not get nutrients from the soil.
they do not get sufficient sunshine.
questions.explanation:
In highly eroded and desolated areas, the topsoil, which contains essential nutrients for plant growth, is lost.

 Without nutrients, trees cannot survive, making option C the correct answer.

questions.questionText: Which of the following, according to paragraph 1, is a result of preserving forest areas?
options: Ruins of the land through processes
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 1 emphasizes that preserving forest areas protects the natural habitat, allowing wildlife to reproduce and thrive. 

Therefore, the correct result of forest preservation is the reproduction of wildlife.

questions.questionText: Which of the following, according to paragraph 2, can be a cause of soil erosion?
options: Planting trees and using modern farming
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 explains that soil erosion is accelerated when farmers cultivate hillsides that are prone to erosion.

 This practice removes the protective cover and exposes the soil, making it susceptible to being washed away.

questions.questionText: According to paragraph 2, which of the following is true?
options: Plants can be planted to suck up water and hold soil even if the earth is too shallow to support long roots.
When the soil is washed away to neighboring countries, land productivity increases.
The preservation of forest areas is not the concern of Ethiopians.
Erosion of the soil is worse than destruction of trees.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 2 emphasizes that soil erosion has long-term and widespread consequences, often more severe than simply cutting down trees.

 It highlights that the loss of soil reduces land productivity and damages the environment, making soil erosion a more serious problem than tree destruction.

questions.questionText: What does 'its' in paragraph 1 refer to?
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 1, the pronoun 'its' refers to the act of preserving natural resources. 

The context discusses the positive outcomes of preservation, such as protecting wildlife and soil, indicating that 'its' points to 'preservation of natural resources.'

questions.questionText:
Section Three Vocabulary: A. Completion. Instructions: Questions from 19-24 are incomplete sentences. There are four alternative words or phrases, A-D, given below each question. Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.

 You should not be so __________ to these late comers; once punished, they should be allowed to attend class.
questions.explanation:
The sentence suggests that while latecomers should be punished, they should still be allowed to attend class.

 Being 'cruel' would mean being excessively harsh and not allowing them back, so the sentence advises against being cruel. Therefore, 'cruel' is the best choice.

questions.questionText: Ethiopia will enjoy a period of peace and __________ in the next few years, this happens if the country ensures law and gives priority to science, technology and innovation.
questions.explanation:
The sentence links peace and a positive outcome with prioritizing science, technology, and innovation.

 The most logical and positive outcome that goes hand-in-hand with peace and development is prosperity, which means being successful in material terms; flourishing economically.

questions.questionText: The weather in Addis Ababa is __________ these days. You cannot tell whether it rains in the morning or in the afternoon.
questions.explanation:
The reason given—'You cannot tell whether it rains in the morning or in the afternoon'—describes a lack of certainty about future events.

 The word that best describes something that cannot be accurately foreseen or foretold is unpredictable.

questions.questionText: __________ by the speech of the new leader, all the people of the Zone elected him to be Member of Parliament.
questions.explanation:
The cause-and-effect relationship in the sentence is that the leader's speech led to a positive action: being elected as Member of Parliament.

 The words 'Offended,' 'Demotivated,' and 'Discouraged' are negative and would lead to a negative or neutral outcome.

Inspired is the only positive choice, meaning the people felt motivated and enthusiastic enough by the speech to elect him.

questions.questionText: On my way home from office, there was high traffic __________ . It took me two hours to get home.
questions.explanation:
The consequence given ('It took me two hours to get home') is a result of heavy, slow-moving traffic.

 The word that specifically means the state of being extremely crowded or blocked with traffic is congestion.

 While a 'freeway' is a type of road, 'traffic congestion' is the condition that causes delays.

questions.questionText: In the annual festival that they hold, the villagers in my area always __________ to fight against the criminals that disturb the people.
questions.explanation:
The villagers commit to a course of action: fighting against criminals.

 The word that means to decide firmly on a course of action or to make a fixed determination is resolve.

 'Meditate,' 'remember,' and 'think' do not convey the sense of making a firm commitment to act.

questions.questionText:
Section Three Vocabulary: B. Substitution. Instructions: For questions 25-30, each sentence has an underlined word or phrase, followed by alternatives A-D. Choose the word or phrase that best corresponds with the meaning of the underlined word or phrase. 

 Houses in cities are not **affordable** for the great majority of the people in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation:
Affordable means being able to be afforded; priced so that one can manage to buy it.

 Among the options, cheap (or inexpensive) is the word closest in meaning to something being within one's financial reach, especially in a context where 'not affordable' means too expensive.

questions.questionText: He asked her to **turn round** several times before he gave her his opinion of her new dress.
questions.explanation:
To turn round means to move in a circle so that one is facing the opposite direction, or to physically spin.

 The word that means to move or cause to move around an axis or a center is rotate.

questions.questionText: Thanks to science and technology, many of our organs are **replaceable**.
questions.explanation:
Replaceable means capable of being replaced.

 In the context of organs, this means that a damaged organ can be substituted with another one.

 The word that captures the idea of being able to be swapped or substituted is exchangeable.

questions.questionText: The teacher announced that the mathematics examination has been **put off** for next week.
questions.explanation: The phrase put off means to postpone, delay, or defer an event to a later time.

questions.questionText: If you go to a new place, your behavior and manner should **harmonize** with that of the people you meet there.
questions.explanation:
To harmonize means to be consistent or compatible with something else.

 The context suggests that one's behavior should fit in or blend with the local people's behavior.

 Integrate means to combine with another thing so that they become a whole, which captures the meaning of blending one's behavior to fit the group.

questions.questionText: Tensions between the two countries are rising quickly. We cannot **rule out** the possibility that war breaks out.
questions.explanation:
To rule out a possibility means to dismiss it, exclude it, or determine that it is impossible or irrelevant.

 Therefore, exclude is the closest synonym to the phrase 'rule out' in this context.

questions.questionText:
Section C: Analogy. Instructions: For questions 31 and 32, two pairs of words are given. Look at the relationship between the two words in each pair and choose the word which forms a similar relationship with the word given next to each pair.

 Mouse is to computer as steering wheel is to ________
questions.explanation:
The relationship is: [Control Device] is to [Machine Controlled].

- A Mouse is used to control a computer.

 - A Steering Wheel is used to control a vehicle (like a car or bus).

questions.questionText: Bed: Sleep:: Stove: __________
questions.explanation:
The relationship is: [Object] is used for [Primary Function].

- A Bed is primarily used for Sleep.

- A Stove is primarily used to Cook.

questions.questionText:
Section Four: Sentence Comprehension. Instructions: For questions 33 and 34, choose the sentence with the closest meaning to the head sentence from the four alternatives given.

 All students but one got above average marks in English?
options: Only one student failed to get above average marks in English
Only one student got the above average mark in English
All students did not get above average marks in English
Everybody got above average mark in English.
questions.explanation:
The phrase 'all students but one' means that every student except one achieved the stated result.

 Therefore, the sentence that conveys the same meaning is that only one student did not get above average marks in English.

questions.questionText: Addis Ababa University, which is the oldest university in the country, has changed its admission policy?
options: Addis Ababa University admits students based on new rules and regulations.
Addis Ababa University has grown old with its admission policy.
Addis Ababa University has a conducive learning atmosphere.
Joining Addis Ababa University has now become easy.
questions.explanation:
To change its admission policy means that the university now has a different set of rules or criteria for admitting students.

 Option A, 'Addis Ababa University admits students based on new rules and regulations,' is the sentence that best captures the meaning of a changed admission policy.

questions.questionText:
Directions: Questions from 35-42 are incomplete sentences with a word or phrase missing. Choose the word or phrase that accurately and clearly fills the blank.

 At first, the suspect did not realize _________ during the interview. Later on, he saw the voice recorder and refused to continue the interview.
questions.explanation:
The correct choice is 'he was being recorded' because the suspect did not initially know that the interview was being captured by a recorder.

 The passive continuous form 'was being recorded' accurately conveys that the recording was happening to him during the interview.

questions.questionText: Unlike last year, only __________ students needed extra help this year; last year we helped almost every one in the class.
questions.explanation:
The key phrase is the contrast: 'Unlike last year,' which is then clarified as 'last year we helped **almost every one.' This means that this year, the number of students needing help must be very small.

 A few (referring to a small, countable number of students) is the best choice to convey this sharp contrast with 'almost every one.'

questions.questionText: We should be involved in sports activities to keep __________ fit and healthy.
questions.explanation:
The subject of the sentence is the plural pronoun 'We'.

 The corresponding reflexive pronoun used to reflect the action back to the plural subject is ourselves.

 The action of keeping fit and healthy is done to 'us'.

questions.questionText: I __________ my homework when you knocked at the door.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'was doing' because the action of doing homework was in progress at the specific past time when the knocking occurred.

 The past continuous tense ('was doing') is used to indicate an ongoing action in the past that was interrupted by another action.

questions.questionText: ___________I do not complain much; my friends often take me for a fool.
questions.explanation:
'In spite of' is correct because it introduces a contrast between two ideas: even though the speaker does not complain much, the friends still think poorly of them.

 It conveys the meaning of 'despite this' or 'although this is the case.

questions.questionText: My English is not good. I __________ advised to study English when I was younger.
questions.explanation:
The correct choice is 'wish I had been' because the speaker is expressing a regret about something in the past that did not happen — specifically, being advised to study English when younger.

 The past perfect form 'had been advised' is used to indicate an unreal past condition.

questions.questionText: I __________ much today if I had learned about money management at my young age.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'would not have worried' because this is a third conditional sentence.

 It refers to a hypothetical situation in the past (learning about money management at a young age) and its consequence in the past (not worrying today).

 The structure 'if + past perfect, would have + past participle' is used for unreal past conditions.

questions.questionText: _____________you ever__________ a chance to visit any historical site in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation:
The correct choice is 'Have/had' because the question is in the present perfect tense, which is used to ask about experiences at any time up to now.

 The structure is 'Have you ever had...?' where 'have' is the auxiliary verb and 'had' is the past participle of 'have.'

questions.questionText: The road project __________ by the construction company next year.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'will be completed' because the sentence describes a future passive action.

 'Will be completed' is the future passive form, indicating that the construction company will finish the road project next year.

questions.questionText: I had enough money , I __________ schools with elevators for visually impaired children.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'would have built' because this is a third conditional sentence.

 It expresses an unreal past condition (having enough money) and its hypothetical past result (building schools).

 The structure 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle' is used for unreal past situations.

questions.questionText: Next year this time, I __________ the freshman program.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'will be nearly complete' because the sentence refers to a future time ('next year this time') and describes the state of the program at that time. 'Will be nearly complete' correctly uses the future simple tense to indicate a future state.

questions.questionText: This year's examination is as good as the one given last year, __________?
questions.explanation:
This is a Tag Question.

 The main verb phrase in the statement is is as good as... (Present Simple using 'to be').

 The tag must use the same auxiliary verb ('is') but be negative because the statement is positive, and the subject is the non-human singular noun 'examination' (represented by 'it').

 Thus, the tag is isn't it.

questions.questionText: I met the girl __________ phone number I was asking for.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'whose' because it is used to show possession. 

The sentence refers to the girl who possesses the phone number, so 'whose' properly connects the noun 'girl' with the noun 'phone number.'

questions.questionText: When you acknowledge people’s contribution to your work, you need not refer __________ his/her name.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'to' because the phrase 'refer to' is the proper collocation in English when mentioning or pointing out something.

 The sentence means you do not need to mention the person's name, so 'refer to his/her name' is grammatically correct.

questions.questionText: __________listening__________Reading are important academic skills students need to develop.
questions.explanation:
This sentence requires a word to be paired with reading that is also an important academic skill.

Listening is the only option that fits this context, completing the phrase 'reading and listening' as key academic skills.

 Options B, C, and D are coordinating conjunctions that are used incorrectly here.

questions.questionText: He __________ his children to school five days a week.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'drives' because the sentence describes a habitual action in the present.

 The simple present tense is used for routines or repeated actions, such as taking children to school regularly.

questions.questionText: My father is not __________old_________  yours; he is only 53 years old.
questions.explanation:
The correct structure for comparison in negative sentences is 'not as + adjective + as.'

 Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'My father is not as old as yours.'

questions.questionText: Lojo is __________ tall girl___________ she can easily touch the ceiling of her classroom.
questions.explanation:
The correct structure is 'such + a + adjective + noun + that.'

 Since 'tall girl' includes a noun, we use 'such a... that.'

 The complete sentence is: 'Lojo is such a tall girl that she can easily touch the ceiling of her classroom.'

questions.questionText: Some students did well on the last week's English test,___________ others scored unsatisfactory marks. I am designing an action research to study the case.
questions.explanation:
'Whereas' is used to show contrast between two clauses.

 The sentence contrasts students who did well with others who scored unsatisfactory marks.

 The other options do not correctly express contrast between two independent clauses.

questions.questionText: My English teacher __________ me repeat the correct answer ten times.
questions.explanation:
The correct structure is 'make + object + base verb.'

 So we say, 'My English teacher made me repeat the correct answer ten times.' 

The other options require different grammatical structures (e.g., 'wanted me to repeat,' 'told me to repeat')

questions.questionText: My history teacher asked me __________what is your nationality?
questions.explanation:
In reported (indirect) speech, the word order changes to statement form (subject + verb), not question form.

 Therefore, we say 'what my nationality is' instead of 'what is my nationality.'

questions.questionText: You __________ go to bed before midnight if you have the habit of getting up late.
questions.explanation:
'Will not' expresses a predictable result based on a habit.

 If you have the habit of getting up late, you will not (are unlikely to) go to bed before midnight. 

It shows a general tendency rather than impossibility. 'Cannot' would suggest impossibility, which is too strong in this context.

questions.questionText: You will start running __________ the bell rings. Otherwise, you will be disqualified from the competition.
questions.explanation:
The sentence indicates that running should begin once the bell has rung. 

'After' correctly shows that the action happens following the bell. 'Till' means up to a time, 'while' means at the same time, and 'during' is used with nouns, not clauses.

questions.questionText: The afternoon sun is __________ hot for school children ________ play outside. They had better stay in their class.
questions.explanation:
The correct structure is 'too + adjective + to + verb.' So the sentence becomes: 'The afternoon sun is too hot for school children to play outside.

' This structure shows that the heat prevents them from playing.

questions.questionText: The lady __________ next to our English teacher is my mother's close friend.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is 'sitting' because it is a present participle used to describe the lady. It functions as a reduced relative clause: 'The lady who is sitting next to our English teacher...' The other options do not fit grammatically in this structure.

questions.questionText: Unlike my friends, who dislike drinking coffee, I __________ go to bed at night without a coffee.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'never' because the sentence emphasizes that, unlike friends, the speaker does not go to bed without coffee.

 'Never' appropriately conveys this habitual impossibility. The other options do not express the intended meaning.

questions.questionText: Committing corruption __________ life imprisonment in several countries in the world.
questions.explanation:
'Leads to' correctly expresses cause and effect. Committing corruption results in or leads to life imprisonment.

 The other options do not convey this causal relationship appropriately.

questions.questionText: I always have much work to do; that is why I __________ have time to listen to music.
questions.explanation:
'Scarcely' means 'hardly' or 'almost not,' which fits the context of having very little time due to being busy.

 The sentence becomes: 'I always have much work to do; that is why I scarcely have time to listen to music.' The other options do not convey this meaning.

questions.questionText:
Section One: Word forms 63 and 64 are on word spelling. From the alternatives A, B, C, D choose the one which is correctly spelt. 
 Choose the one which is correctly spelt.

 Instruction: Section One: Word forms 63 and 64 are on word spelling. From the alternatives A, B, C, D choose the one which is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation:
'Expenditure' is the correct spelling.

 The other options contain spelling errors: 

-'traditionial' should be 'traditional,'

- 'particularily' should be 'particularly,' and

- 'fotograph' should be 'photograph.

questions.questionText: Choose the one which is correctly spelt.
questions.explanation: 'Repetition' is the correctly spelled word. The other options are misspelled: 'paralism' should be 'parallelism,' 'suffication' should be 'suffocation,' and 'inteligibility' should be 'intelligibility.'

questions.questionText: Section Two: Punctuation and Capitalization. Instructions: Questions 65-67 are on punctuation and capitalization. From the given alternatives A - D, choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized, . Choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized.
options: Tadesse and Fanuel are good friends. They study their lessons together and help each other.
Tadesse and Fanuel are good friends; They study their lessons together and help each other.
tadesse and fanuel are good friends, they study their lessons together and help each other.
Tadesse and fanuel are good friends They study their lessons together and help each other!
questions.explanation:
The first option is correct because it properly capitalizes the names 'Tadesse' and 'Fanuel,' uses a period to separate two complete sentences, and correctly capitalizes the beginning of the second sentence.

 The other options contain punctuation or capitalization errors

questions.questionText: Choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized.
options: Ethiopia is a rich country endowed with many natural resources. In addition it has many diversified cultures and very friendly people.
Ethiopia is a rich country endowed with many natural resources. In addition, it has many diversified cultures and very friendly people
Ethiopia is a rich country endowed with many natural resources. In addition it has many diversified cultures and very friendly people.
Ethiopia is a rich country endowed with many natural resources. In addition, it has many diversified cultures and very friendly people.
questions.explanation:
The correct sentence includes a comma after the transitional phrase 'In addition,' and ends with a period.

 The other options either omit the comma or the final period.

questions.questionText: Choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized.
options: Hello Kenyan National Hotel. can I help you?
Hello, Kenyan National Hotel, can I help you?
Hello, Kenyan National Hotel! Can I help you?
Hello Kenyan National Hotel. Can I help you?
questions.explanation:
The correct option properly capitalizes words, uses commas to separate the greeting from the name, includes correct punctuation after the greeting, and capitalizes the question correctly.

 The other options contain capitalization or punctuation errors.

questions.questionText: Arrange the jumbled words/phrases to form a correct English sentence. (Jumbled: am/as/think/I/not/I/you/stupid/am/you.)
options: I am not as I think am stupid as you.
As you think I am not stupid as I am.
I am not as you think as I am.
I am not as stupid as you think I am.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence structure is 'not as + adjective + as.' The properly arranged sentence is: 'I am not as stupid as you think I am.'

questions.questionText: Arrange the jumbled words/phrases to form a correct English sentence. ( who/a/clever/teacher/in/school/our/Ato Tadesse/got/has/a/scholarship/is.)
options: Ato Tadesse, in our school, has got a scholarship who is a clever teacher.
Ato Tadesse, who is a clever teacher in our school, has got a scholarship.
Ato Tadesse is a clever teacher in school who has got our a scholarship.
Ato Tadesse has got a scholarship, who is a clever teacher , in our school.
questions.explanation:
The correct sentence uses a relative clause ('who is a clever teacher in our school') to describe Ato Tadesse.

 The commas properly set off the non-restrictive clause, making the sentence grammatically correct and well structured.

questions.questionText: Arrange the jumbled words/phrases to form a correct English sentence. (Jumbled: in/the/science/laboratory/teacher/and/students/both/together/working/the/are/the.)
options: The students and the teacher together are both working in the science laboratory.
The students are working and both the teacher together in the science laboratory.
Both in the science laboratory are working together the teacher and the students.
Both the teacher and the students are working together in the science laboratory.
questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'Both... and...' followed by the plural verb 'are working.' The sentence is grammatically correct and logically arranged.

questions.questionText:
Arrange the sentences (a-d) to form a coherent paragraph. 

a. Arable farming refers to growing crops. 

b This farming type refers to keeping sheep and cattle. 

c. The second farming type is pastoral farming. 

d. Arable and pastoral farming are commonly known farming types.
questions.explanation:
- Sentence d introduces the two farming types.

- Sentence a explains arable farming first. 

- Sentence c introduces the second type, pastoral farming. 

- Sentence b then explains pastoral farming, making the paragraph logical and coherent.

questions.questionText:
Arrange the sentences (a-d) to form a coherent paragraph. 

a. Hanna is a very charming and sociable girl whom everybody likes. 

b Finally, she works in an international supermarket as a saleswoman. She is always smiling and appears to be happy with her job. 

c. She is only in her late twenties. She usually wears jeans that visibly show the shape of her body. Above her waist, she wears a white nylon T-shirt that makes her breasts appear more visible and attractive. 

d. To begin with, she is tall and has a slim waist that makes her quite attractive.
questions.explanation:
Sentence a introduces Hanna generally. Sentence d begins describing her physical appearance.

 Sentence c continues with more detailed description. Sentence b concludes by describing her job and personality at work, making the paragraph coherent.

questions.questionText:
Arrange the sentences (a-d) to form a coherent paragraph. 

a. Many people believe education is the key to success in life. 

b. These people list names of several intellectuals who struggle to make in the end to breath on their salaries. 

c. As examples, they mention highly educated people who have become rich. 

d. Others contend that education only leads people to poverty.
questions.explanation:
Sentence a introduces the common belief that education is the key to success.

 Sentence c gives examples supporting this belief. Sentence b then provides counterexamples of educated people who struggle financially. Sentence d concludes with the opposing view that education can lead to poverty, creating a coherent flow from belief, support, counterexample, to contrasting opinion.

questions.questionText:
Arrange the sentences (a-d) to form a coherent paragraph. (A. Three of their children are girls 

B. His wife wizero Mulu, is younger than him by 2 years

C. Ato Lemma and Wizero Mulu have four children.

D.Ato Lemma is a thirty-year-old person in my community.
questions.explanation:
Sentence d introduces Ato Lemma by age. Sentence b introduces his wife, Wizero Mulu.

 Sentence c mentions that they have four children. Sentence a provides additional detail that three of their children are girls, creating a logical and coherent paragraph.

questions.questionText:
Identify the type of paragraph writing that is most likely for the following text: 
"First of all, the death penalty should be only resort to killing people and spend the rest of their lives jail ."Moreover, if the death penalty committed against them would like to take revenge on the criminal and this makes chaos in society'. This is what paragraph writing that is most likely:
questions.explanation: The paragraph presents a point of view on the death penalty and provides reasons to support that opinion, which is characteristic of an argumentative paragraph.

questions.questionText:
Identify the type of paragraph writing that is most likely for the following text: 
Digestion starts in the mouth. This is called mechanical digestion as there is not any kind of chemical involved in the process.It is simply as the saliva is broken down into smaller pieces and the food is swallowed.The other type of digestion is chemical digestion. It is in stomach that this digestion takes place. The above paragraph are most likely taken from :
questions.explanation:
The paragraph explains the process of digestion step by step, providing factual information without expressing opinions or telling a story. 

This is characteristic of an expository paragraph.

questions.questionText: Eden is in her late twenties. She is of medium height. She has an average weight that fits her height, she respects people, and she is very polite and friendly.From which of the following paragraph writing types is the above sentences most likely?
questions.explanation:
The paragraph focuses on describing Eden’s physical appearance and personality traits in detail.

 It provides sensory and characteristic details, which is typical of a descriptive paragraph.

questions.questionText:

questions.questionText:

You could learn active and passive voices.

questions.questionText:

You:__________
options: I am sure today's children won't expect a job from the government
In my opinion, none of a working age will be unemployed
I think unemployment is a universal problem these days
Think about today; tomorrow is another day
questions.explanation: The response appropriately expresses an opinion about unemployment, matching the question asking for a perspective on future unemployment.

questions.questionText:
Teacher:___________

options: It isn't very disappointing to see students in the classroom without their uniform
Is it very disappointing to see students in the classroom without their uniform
When do we see students in the classroom without their uniform
Why do we see students in the classroom without their uniform
questions.explanation:

 The correct form is a question: 'Is it very disappointing to see students in the classroom without their uniform?' to which the parent responds in agreement.

 Wife: _____________ Has the cause been known?
options: Look after yourself on the road.
I am sorry to say this.

 The appropriate response expressing shock or sympathy is 'What a terrible news!'

questions.questionText:

options: going to college is not mandatory
perhaps we need to learn further
perhaps it is one among the few

 'Perhaps it is one among the few' suggests that education is important but not the only way to live a better life.

questions.questionText:
Neighbor: Today's youths have a much wider access to information than those who lived in the past.

Father: Yes, but __________
options: it is good to remember those who lived in the past were less intelligent
the trouble is they are indiscriminate in their choice of information
we should appreciate the unlimited interest of today's youth
the main point is they do not read all that comes their way
questions.explanation:
The father's response acknowledges the neighbor's point but adds a caution.

 He points out that although youths have more access, they may not select information wisely, making this the most coherent continuation.
